citations.review_text:
👍 RECOMMENDED
🦇 The Absolute Peak of Superhero Gaming
Nearly a decade later, Batman: Arkham Knight still sets the gold standard for AAA action games. It’s visual perfection, pure gameplay dopamine, and the ultimate "Be the Batman" simulator.

Why it’s pure PEAK:
🎨 Next-Gen Visuals: Rain-slicked Gotham looks better than most modern AAA releases.

👊 God-Tier Combat: Smooth, brutal, and fast-paced Freeflow mechanics at their absolute prime.

🏎️ Peak Traversal: Dive-bombing from the sky straight into the Batmobile never gets old.

🎭 Legendary Story: Unforgettable performances by Kevin Conroy and Mark Hamill.

Pros: Unmatched atmosphere, godly combat, jaw-dropping graphics.

Cons: Too many Riddler trophies, a few too many tank fights.

VERDICT: 10 / 10 — A Timeless Masterpiece

[b]If you want to feel exactly like Batman—brooding in the rain, grappling up skyscrapers, and breaking the collarbones of petty criminals in glorious, fluid motion—this game is the absolute pinnacle. Even a decade after its release, Gotham looks so stunning and rain-slicked that it puts most modern releases to shame. The free-flow combat and predator stealth are perfected here, making you feel like a terrifying mythical creature right up until you remember you have to do your taxes.

The only real catch is that Rocksteady really wanted you to love the Batmobile. Need to solve an ancient riddle? Batmobile. Track a serial killer? Batmobile. By hour 30, I wasn’t sure if I was playing a Batman game or a very dark, very expensive episode of Pimp My Ride. You will also spend an ungodly amount of time hunting down 243 green trophies just because Edward Nygma built a literal subterranean drag-racing circuit to prove he's smarter than you.

Despite the aggressive over-reliance on tank battles and a "twist" villain identity you can see coming from outer space, it’s a brilliant, atmospheric conclusion to the trilogy. Buy it, play it, and try not to think too hard when the game tells you a thug is merely "unconscious" after getting blasted by a 5-ton tank rocket. 9/10.[/b]

citations.review_text: Animations are very well done and combat flows like water once you master it.

I have never seen a game get in its own way so much. You're stopped every 5 feet to do some garbage with your batmobile, or listen to a needlessly long phone call. The actual combat, when the game deigns that you can actually do that, is great and feels very fluid and fun. It's a shame the game keeps shoehorning the batmobile into places it doesn't belong.

Ponto Positivo:​ Batman: Arkham Knight é um jogo impressionante que consegue elevar o nível da franquia em diversos aspectos. Visualmente, o jogo é impecável, com uma Gotham City sombria, chuvosa e extremamente imersiva que realmente faz o jogador se sentir na pele do Homem-Morcego. A jogabilidade evoluiu muito, oferecendo combates fluidos, uma exploração vertical incrível e uma narrativa que te prende do início ao fim. É, sem dúvidas, uma experiência indispensável e muito interessante.
​No entanto, mesmo sendo um jogo excelente, ele comete alguns erros graves que prejudicam a experiência do jogador, principalmente na construção de um vilão e no excesso de tarefas repetitivas.
​
Pontos Negativos: As Minhas Críticas

1. O Desperdício do Cavaleiro de Arkham
​A grande decepção da campanha gira em torno da postura do Cavaleiro de Arkham como antagonista. Durante a história, ele se comporta de maneira covarde: em vez de bater de frente com o Batman, ele passa o tempo todo se escondendo atrás de um exército militar, tanques e capangas. Essa dinâmica tira toda a graça da rivalidade.
​
O ponto crítico acontece na revelação de sua identidade como Jason Todd (o Capuz Vermelho). Nos quadrinhos e em animações, o confronto entre os dois é épico, doloroso e pessoal, onde eles se enfrentam de igual para igual, no mano a mano e sem armas. No jogo, isso se perde. O vilão só usa armas de longe e foge do combate físico, transformando o que deveria ser uma luta final emocionante em um jogo de esconde-esconde onde ele fica de longe com um rifle. Reduzir um personagem tão letal a um comandante que não "peita" o Batman foi um erro de desenvolvimento.

​2. O Exagero Surtado do Charada
​Outro grande problema do jogo é a mecânica das missões do Charada. Embora faça sentido ele usar pistas e enigmas para desafiar o Batman, a Rocksteady pesou a mão de uma forma completamente absurda na quantidade de desafios.
​Quantidade exagerada: Exigir que o jogador encontre centenas de troféus …

citations.review_text: This isn't a Batman game it's a Batmobile game, I swear to god you spend more time shooting unmanned Tanks than you do anything else

Extremely conflicted about this game.

On one side it easily has the most in depth and fun gameplay of the Arkham franchise. On the other... you have everything else.

The Batmobile combat sucks, it's repetitive, not remotely challenging and lasts for too long.

It has the worst story in the franchise because for some reason they didn't want to get Paul Dini back (Origins at least had the excuse of being made by a separate smaller studio).

Most of the DLCs suck and are way too short, you can probably beat all of them in about an hour (don't buy the Catwoman DLC).

Overall this game just pisses me off because it could've genuinely been one of the greatest games of all time if it wasn't for stupid decisions by the studio.

6/10 and all of those points are because of the base gameplay

I hate the Batmobile in this game, but outside of the mandatory tank sections and the bloody racetracks this is probably the best Batman: Arkham game.

There aren't a lot of mandatory tank sections and the racetracks can be ignored (♥♥♥♥ do they suck).

Batman: Arkham Knight is the ultimate conclusion to the legendary Arkham trilogy. It delivers an unmatched superhero power fantasy, dropping you into a stunning, rain-soaked Gotham City that feels alive and atmospheric. The signature "Freeflow" combat is at its absolute peak here—fluid, brutal, and incredibly satisfying. If you want to truly be the Batman, this is the best it will ever get.
​🟢 Pros
​Peak Combat & Stealth: The Freeflow combat and Predator stealth mechanics are refined to absolute perfection, offering total tactical freedom.
​Stunning Visuals: Even years after its release, the game looks absolutely breathtaking with incredible rain effects, animations, and attention to detail.
​The Ultimate Playground: Gotham City is massive, dark, and filled with secrets, Riddler trophies, and excellent side missions featuring classic villains.
​Incredible Story: A dark, psychological narrative that pushes Batman to his absolute limits, featuring a brilliant performance by the Joker.
​🔴 Cons
​Overused Batmobile: While driving the Batmobile is fun at first, the game forces you into too many repetitive tank-battle sections that slow down the pacing.
​Predictable Twist: Without spoiling anything, the identity of the "Arkham Knight" is quite easy to guess early on for anyone familiar with Batman lore.
​PC Port Legacy: While it runs beautifully now on modern hardware, you might still encounter occasional minor optimization glitches in specific areas.
​Final Verdict: 9.5/10
​Highly Recommended. A masterpiece of the superhero genre. Minor Batmobile fatigue aside, it is an essential game that every action-adventure fan needs to experience.

An awesome finale to the Arkham trilogy. One of my favorite games of all time. 

My only issue with the game is that it relies heavily on the batmobile. Don't get me wrong, the batmobile controls really well and it's really fun to drive around the city and mow every obstacle in your way, but i think there is a little too much of it. Like for example, there is a side mission where you have to disable bombs scattered around Gotham with your batmobile. When you start to hack the bomb, it starts an encounter where you have to destroy the militia drones. First it is okay. There is only couple of them, but when you are disabling the last bombs there comes like 50 of them. And i think there is way too many bombs for the gameplay they offer. They could have cut some of the bombs out and made the Deacon Blackfire side mission longer. 

The combat feels super fluid in this game. They fleshed out the already great Arkham city combat and gave you even more gadgets to use. The fear multitakedown is really great addition to the predator segments and let's the encounters be larger in enemy size and location. 

The DLC stories and missions are really good. The season of infamy missions are all good and give closure to some of the best characters in the trilogy. I especially liked the Mr.Freeze and Raz al Ghul missions. The Mr.Freeze missions captures what makes him a compelling character and an interesting villain and gives him and his wife Nora the most beautiful ending they could have. Then there are the extra story DLC. All of them are quite short except for one, but i'll get to that in a bit. The short ones are all good for their length. The Catwoman and Harley Quinn stories are quite underwhelming, which i hate to say because Harley is my favorite DC character. The Nightwing and Robin DLC are good and i really like the voice acting and dialogue in the Robin DLC. The longer DLC story A Matter of family is amazing. Extremely conflicted about this game.

On one side it easily has the most in depth and fun gameplay of the Arkham franchise. On the other... you have everything else.

The Batmobile combat sucks, it's repetitive, not remotely challenging and lasts for too long.

It has the worst story in the franchise because for some reason they didn't want to get Paul Dini back (Origins at least had the excuse of being made by a separate smaller studio).

Most of the DLCs suck and are way too short, you can probably beat all of them in about an hour (don't buy the Catwoman DLC).

6/10 and all of those points are because of the base gameplay

Phenomenal combat--best I have EVER seen. So fluid and the combos are crazy. The story is great, some of the side challenges are annoying, like finding all the firefighters; it took me looking for over two hours to find the last one on founders island. All the extension missions are really short, but fun none the less. I really love this game, and can't think of anything that would make it unplayable!

It is difficult to really articulate just how good this game is. Some people may not enjoy how prevalent the batmobile is, but this game had to add something big to set it apart from City and Asylum. I quite enjoy using the batmobile and the way the villains operate in this game, it makes sense to have it.

Seeing Gotham in the rainy night with bad guys absolutely everywhere to beat up really makes it feel like you are Batman. The free flow combat has never been better and the predator sections are peak Batman gameplay. Every aspect of the game is molded to Batman's character perfectly. The way he speaks, moves, fights, and his interactions with every character are a shining example to how Batman should be portrayed. The detective aspects throughout the game really go to show how he holds the title of World's Greatest Detective.

The DLCs are all phenomenal and make me wish we had a dedicated game for each and every one of the protagonists who have a DLC. Robin, Harley, Catwoman, Batgirl, Nightwing, and Red Hood all deserve much more than just the short, maybe 30 minute DLC each one gets. The exception is Batgirl, whose DLC is more fleshed out and takes about an hour and a half to finish give or take. Still, it leaves you wanting more. 

The look of the game cannot be understated. More than a decade has passed and this game blows many modern titles out of the water in my opinion as far as graphics go. Truly, something was lost in the gaming world after a certain time. With how big the map is, it's constantly raining, and everything still manages to look sharp, detailed and the game runs well over 60 fps, it makes you wonder why so many modern games struggle to tick all of the boxes without needing 64gb of RAM.

The one and only downside in my opinion, as many other reviews state, is the 243 Riddler trophies that you need to get to unlock the 100% ending. 243 is excessive, especially considering none of them are very difficult. I know people had complaints about City…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the PC port as suffering from unplayable crashes or requiring configuration and driver updates to function correctly.

citations.review_text:
It feels weird not being able to recommend what I consider to be a fantastic game overall. Seriously, I remembered the Batmobile sections as very clunky and annoying to navigate but playing it now I had so much fun with it that I made it a point to get from one point of the map to other by car rather than flying, even after unlocking the grapple accelerator abilities. The game is just as smooth as it was in Origins, the graphics are unbelievable even after 10 years, and the story, while predictable, benefits from surprisingly sharp writing for the most part (Shout-out to the Riddler, Joker and Scarecrow dialogues) with the exception of the Arkham Knight which has to be the worst kept secret and the most underwhelming reveal of the 2010's. The rogue gallery is, as always, one of the highlights here and if you're going to play this game, I'd recommend getting the additional story DLCs for the main campaign (I may be biased since my GOAT Croc is in one of those).
So if the gameplay is fantastic, the writing is good and the graphics are fun, why can I not recommend this game?
The PC port is unplayable. I scoured both Reddit, Steam and even GameFAQs for fixes that would help me avoid constant crashes and nothing worked. Trust me, I tried every piece of advice the Internet had to offer. The crashes were also REALLY irregular. I heard some people got stuck at specific sections and I wish that had been my case so I could've maybe identified what the issue was. But instead my game froze and crashed at the strangest times. Arkham Knight would crash sometimes without even the game launching at times, while at other times, I could play 1-2 hours before the software shut down. But despite the game being fantastic, I was in constant fear of the game crashing (sometimes crashing my PC as well) and that very much ruined my enjoyment of it.
As a final note, Mark Hamill, despite being an important part of my childhood through these games, has shown himself to turn a blind eye to w…

BEWARE! All of the Arkham Batman PC Ports require configuring before they will work on your computer. Ensure all of your drivers are up to date, you have the right physx installed, and proper directx.
If not, you game will either crash or refuse to launch. Be ready to refund the game if necessary.

Otherwise, this port is identical to the console experience and I highly recommend the game. The best gameplay in the series yet.

citations.review_text:
11 years later and this game STILL has some of the best graphics in the gaming industry.
The story is not as good as the previous game but when compared to Arkham City that's a hard game to follow up. Gameplay is vastly improved in this one and no you're not stuck in the batmobile but there is boss fights that I wish weren't batmobile fights (deathstroke boss). Amazing based game that makes you feel like that batman. 8/10

One of the best "git gud" games I've played. Surprised it also doesn't have the "overwhelmingly positive" status of the previous 2.

Better graphics than the past 2 games.

Animations are very well done and combat flows like water once you master it.

Finding all the collectables was both a chore and rewarding at the same time as you need the XP to get upgrades for Batman. In terms of grind I could only give a sigh of relief as it isn't close to as grindy as the previous game to 100%.

The atmosphere is dark and fits perfectly with a Batman game.

Sounds are great.
Music is great and fits with the game and atmosphere.

Better in every aspect than the previous 2 games in my opinion.

As a former hater of this game I’ve really warmed up to it over the years. It’s true that the story is a huge step down from city and the bat tank (not the car just the tank aspect of it) just isn’t fun enough to justify how frequently you use it, but I believe the rest of the game is top tier stuff, the combat has much more to it compared to the previous entries and the same is the case for the stealth, enemies have so many ways to counter your tactics once you do them enough almost like how Mr. Freeze worked last time around, the “endless knight” challenge map really shows this off as once you get far enough the enemies will have traps set for you all over the map.
Visually this is probably the best looking game ever made and it’s over a decade old.
If you’re a fan of the previous entries and either haven’t played this one or remember it being a disappointment I’d say give it (another) go because while it’s the most flawed in the trilogy there’s definitely a lot to love.

It's not a bad game but it's a meh Batman Arkham game. The binary YES NO of Steam really doesnt fit.

**YOU WILL NOT GET AN ENDING FOR THE GAME UNTIL YOU COLLECT ALL RIDDLER OBJECTS AND COMPLETE EVERY SIDE MISSION**

It has so many good things going for it, the combat feels brutal, Gotham feels like Gotham, visually it's great, sound design is amazing and the voice acting cast is absolutely stacked.

However the devs made serious missteps. There are 315 Riddler related side objects such as destroyable objects, riddle, trophies, and other victims. The problem is that these are all incredibly boring. For the victim you literally just fly a batarang around and then shoot them with the stun gun.
-I am aware that this is less than the 400 in the previous game however that game is significantly smaller in map size with multiple trophies being basically on top of one another as opposed to across the massive map.

The game is more about the batmobile than it is about batman. They entirely constructed several boss fights, entire puzzles, and massive sections of the story exclusively dedicated to the batmobile which after a few fights really loses the cool factor and just become overused.

Augmented reality challenges are added to the game so you can earn upgrade points. These challenges are so stupid they require you do perform multiple random tasks in the particular challenge to the point it makes them unfun and just work to do.


---SPOILERS FOR VILLAINS INVOLVED IN THE GAME BELOW--

There are multiple boss fights where you don't even really do anything. 

Two-Face makes you clear out multiple small predators maps again and again. 

Firefly you chase around in the batmobile literally waiting for him to run out of fuel, 

Manbat you fly around and chase with your cape, 

the killer croc fight is beat a bunch of dudes, build up a counter, do a qte, and repeat (IMO a far worse fight than the blackgate fight),
